holding_summary: A married woman who leased a farm and, while living on it, ran a boarding-house taking in 25 to 50 summer and year-round boarders was held entitled, under the Married Persons' Property Act of June 3, 1887, to the earnings of that boarding-house business as her separate property, free from seizure by her husband's creditors. The court applied the same reasoning to the products of the farm she operated. The Supreme Court affirmed judgment for the wife on the sheriff's interpleader.
